disposition_reason: Table 2 prints aluminum, arsenic, cadmium, mercury and lead (ug/kg) for each of 12 top-selling retail matcha powders sold in Thailand, plus the overall mean.

study.design: Laboratory-based descriptive survey of top-selling retail matcha powders with health risk assessment
study.market: general stores and online in Thailand; purposive sampling of top-selling products (over 1,000 units/month)
study.method: About 1 g microwave-digested with nitric acid and hydrogen peroxide; ICP-MS at Chulalongkorn University research instrument center
study.qa: Triplicate analyses; no CRM, recovery or LOD reported

controls.comparator: Thai-produced culinary product (07) vs Japanese products
controls.outcome: Pb 1,041.54 ug/kg in product 07 vs 184.05-725.19 ug/kg in the 11 Japanese products

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Exposure at 5 g/day matcha, 57.57 kg body weight
regulatory_or_exposure.value: HQ Al 0.188, Cd 0.0032, Hg 0.0018; MOE As 801.4, Pb 18.0 (BMDL10 0.63 ug/kg bw/day)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Thai Ministry of Public Health Notification No. 414 (2020) cited for contaminant limits

unresolved: Purchase dates not reported (Table 1 lists best-before dates only).
No LOD, CRM or recovery data; 'all five metals detected in every sample' cannot be checked against an LOD.
Authors interpret a lead MOE of 18.0 as no significant concern; the paper's own criterion is MOE > 1.
Thai-language paper without a DOI; peer review not verified. Author names in Thai script; romanisation not stated.
Brand names in Table 1 are omitted; products coded 01-12.
